newsitem.title: JAPAN: Alaska LNG exports to start by 2007 - Alaska senator.
newsitem.headline: Alaska LNG exports to start by 2007 - Alaska senator.

text.p: Liquefied natural gas (LNG) production and exports from Alaska's North Slope are expected to start by 2007, Alaska Senator Frank Murkowski said on Friday.

Feasibility studies for the $14 billion project with an annual output capacity of 15 million tonnes are being conducted by Atlantic Richfield Co, Exxon Corp and British Petroleum Co Plc, majority owners of the giant Prudhoe Bay oil and gas field, Murkowski told a news conference at the U.S. Embassy in Tokyo.
The exports would start "in the year 2005 to 2007, when we anticipate Japan, Korea, Taiwan and possibly China would have a capability to utilise that significant volume", he said.
Murkowski, chairman of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, was visiting Japan after trips to Hong Kong and Taiwan.
Japanese natural gas traders said declining crude output from the North Slope has made Alaska look increasingly at the potential of selling natural gas to Asian customers.
Japan, the world's largest LNG buyer, imported 43 million tonnes of LNG in 1995, accounting for about 63 percent of all LNG cargoes traded on the international market in that year.
